lines.say: You stop going to the gym for months. Your muscles shrink. Game over?
Not quite. Your muscles have a memory.
To grow, each muscle fiber needs more control centers, called nuclei.
So stem cells fuse into the fiber and hand over their nuclei.
Then you quit. The fiber shrinks... but in mouse studies, the extra nuclei stayed.
They wait inside the fiber, for months.
So when you come back, the builders are already there.
In one study, women stopped training for about seven months and lost much of their strength.
They got it back in just six weeks.
So coming back is always faster than starting. Don't quit... but if you do, come back.
